workflow.name: AWS Network Troubleshooting
workflow.description: Guided AWS network troubleshooting using packet-path and configuration-state reasoning.

ec2_no_internet.title: EC2 Cannot Reach Internet
ec2_no_internet.description: Use when an EC2 instance cannot reach an internet destination.

cannot_connect_ec2.title: Cannot Connect to EC2
cannot_connect_ec2.description: Use when a client cannot establish connectivity to an EC2 instance.

vpc_to_vpc_failure.title: VPC-to-VPC Traffic Failure
vpc_to_vpc_failure.description: Use when resources in different VPCs cannot communicate.

onprem_to_aws_failure.title: On-Premises to AWS Failure
onprem_to_aws_failure.description: Use when traffic between an on-premises network and AWS is failing.

check_ec2_network_state.title: Check EC2 Network State
check_ec2_network_state.purpose: Confirm the instance and its network interface are in the expected operational state before troubleshooting routing or security controls.
recommended_checks: Confirm the EC2 instance is running
Confirm the expected ENI is attached
Confirm the expected private IPv4 address
For public internet connectivity, determine whether the instance has a public IPv4 address or Elastic IP
Identify the subnet containing the ENI
Identify the security groups associated with the ENI

check_subnet_route.title: Check Subnet Route
check_subnet_route.purpose: Verify that the subnet route table sends the destination toward the expected next hop.
recommended_checks: Identify the route table associated with the EC2 subnet
Check the route that matches the destination IP or prefix
Confirm the next hop is the expected target
For internet traffic, determine whether the subnet is intended to be public or private
Check for a more specific route that may override the expected path

check_public_internet_path.title: Check Public Internet Path
check_public_internet_path.purpose: Verify that a public subnet instance has the addressing and routing needed to reach the internet through an Internet Gateway.
recommended_checks: Confirm the subnet route table has 0.0.0.0/0 pointing to an Internet Gateway
Confirm the Internet Gateway is attached to the correct VPC
Confirm the EC2 network interface has a public IPv4 address or Elastic IP
Confirm the instance private IP and public IP mapping are as expected
After the route and public addressing are confirmed, continue to Security Group checks

check_private_internet_path.title: Check Private Internet Path
check_private_internet_path.purpose: Verify that a private subnet uses the expected NAT path for outbound internet connectivity.
recommended_checks: Confirm the private subnet route table has 0.0.0.0/0 pointing to the expected NAT Gateway
Confirm the NAT Gateway is in an available state
Confirm the NAT Gateway is located in the intended public subnet
Confirm the NAT Gateway public subnet has a default route to an Internet Gateway
Confirm the Internet Gateway is attached to the VPC
Check for more specific routes that could override the NAT Gateway path
After the NAT path is confirmed, continue to Security Group checks

check_security_group.title: Check Security Group
check_security_group.purpose: Verify that the security groups associated with the EC2 network interface allow the required traffic.
recommended_checks: Identify every security group attached to the EC2 network interface
For inbound connectivity, verify the required protocol and destination port are allowed from the expected source
For outbound connectivity, verify the required destination and protocol are allowed
Check whether the rule uses an IP CIDR, prefix list, or another security group as the source or destination
Verify that the source address seen by the EC2 instance matches what the security group rule expects
Remember that security groups are stateful, so return traffic for an allowed connection does not require a separate reverse-direction rule

check_network_acl.title: Check Network ACL
check_network_acl.purpose: Verify that the subnet network ACL permits both the forward and return traffic required by the connection.
recommended_checks: Identify the network ACL associated with the EC2 subnet
Review inbound rules in rule-number order
Review outbound rules in rule-number order
Confirm the required protocol is permitted
Confirm the service port is permitted in the appropriate direction
Confirm return traffic and required ephemeral ports are permitted
Look for a lower-numbered deny rule that matches before the expected allow rule
Confirm the source and destination CIDRs match the actual packet path

check_flow_evidence.title: Collect AWS Network Evidence
check_flow_evidence.purpose: Use AWS network observability tools to confirm whether the configured path is reachable and whether traffic is being accepted or rejected.
recommended_checks: Use Reachability Analyzer to test the expected source-to-destination path
Review the path explanation and identify any route table, security group, network ACL, gateway, peering, or Transit Gateway component reported as blocking the path
Review VPC Flow Logs at the ENI, subnet, or VPC level for the source and destination traffic
Check whether the relevant flow is marked ACCEPT or REJECT
Correlate the Flow Log timestamp with the actual connectivity test
Remember that Reachability Analyzer evaluates configuration and does not transmit test packets
If Reachability Analyzer reports a valid path but traffic still fails, continue with workload, operating-system, return-path, or application-level checks

ec2_network_failure.title: EC2 Network State Problem
ec2_network_failure.purpose: The instance or its primary network interface is not in the expected state, so higher-layer routing and security troubleshooting should pause here.
likely_causes: EC2 instance is not running
Expected ENI is not attached
Unexpected private IP address
Wrong subnet
Wrong network interface selected for the workload
Unexpected security group association
recommended_checks: Confirm the EC2 instance state
Confirm the expected ENI is attached
Verify the ENI private IPv4 address
Verify the subnet ID
Verify the security groups attached to the ENI
Correct the instance or ENI state before continuing with route troubleshooting

public_ip_failure.title: Public IP Addressing Problem
public_ip_failure.purpose: The public-subnet path requires appropriate public IPv4 addressing for direct IPv4 internet communication through an Internet Gateway.
likely_causes: Instance has no public IPv4 address
Elastic IP is not associated with the expected network interface
Public IP is associated with the wrong instance or ENI
The subnet was expected to auto-assign public IPv4 addresses but does not
recommended_checks: Verify the EC2 private and public IPv4 addressing
Verify Elastic IP association if one is used
Confirm the public address belongs to the intended ENI
Confirm the subnet design is intended to provide direct public internet access

internet_gateway_failure.title: Internet Gateway Path Problem
internet_gateway_failure.purpose: The expected public internet path through the Internet Gateway is missing or misconfigured.
likely_causes: No Internet Gateway attached to the VPC
Wrong Internet Gateway associated with the design
Subnet route table does not send internet traffic to the Internet Gateway
A more specific route sends traffic somewhere else
recommended_checks: Verify an Internet Gateway is attached to the VPC
Verify the subnet route table
Confirm the expected internet route targets the Internet Gateway
Check for more specific routes that override the expected internet path

nat_gateway_failure.title: NAT Gateway Path Problem
nat_gateway_failure.purpose: The private-subnet internet path through the NAT Gateway is not usable.
likely_causes: NAT Gateway is not available
Private subnet route does not point to the intended NAT Gateway
NAT Gateway is deployed in the wrong subnet
NAT Gateway public subnet does not have a usable Internet Gateway path
Security or subnet controls are blocking the expected traffic
The traffic uses a protocol or path not supported by the intended NAT design
recommended_checks: Verify NAT Gateway state
Verify the private subnet default route
Verify the NAT Gateway subnet
Verify the NAT Gateway subnet has an Internet Gateway route
Verify the VPC Internet Gateway attachment
Check security and Network ACL behavior along the path

routing_failure.title: AWS Routing Failure
routing_failure.purpose: The AWS route table does not provide the expected path toward the destination.
likely_causes: Destination route is missing
Route points to the wrong target
A more specific route overrides the expected route
Wrong route table is associated with the subnet
Expected propagated route is absent
Return route is missing on another routing domain
recommended_checks: Identify the route table actually associated with the source subnet
Find the most specific route matching the destination
Verify the target is correct
Check propagated routes where applicable
Verify the return path from the destination side

security_group_failure.title: Security Group Failure
security_group_failure.purpose: The resource security group does not allow the traffic required by the application path.
likely_causes: Required inbound rule is missing
Required outbound rule is missing
Source CIDR is incorrect
Destination CIDR is incorrect
Wrong protocol or destination port
Traffic source address is different from what the rule expects
Wrong security group is attached to the ENI
recommended_checks: Identify all security groups attached to the ENI
Verify protocol and port
Verify source/destination CIDR or security-group reference
Verify the address actually seen by the resource
Remember that security groups are stateful

network_acl_failure.title: Network ACL Failure
network_acl_failure.purpose: The subnet Network ACL is blocking the forward path, return path, or required ephemeral traffic.
likely_causes: Inbound traffic denied
Outbound traffic denied
Return traffic not permitted
Required ephemeral ports are not permitted
A lower-numbered deny rule matches before the intended allow rule
CIDR in the ACL does not match the actual source or destination
recommended_checks: Review inbound rules in rule-number order
Review outbound rules in rule-number order
Verify protocol and service port
Verify required return traffic
Verify ephemeral-port requirements for the actual workload
Check the first matching rule in each direction

analyze_aws_blocking_component.title: Reachability Analyzer Found a Blocking Component
analyze_aws_blocking_component.purpose: Use the Reachability Analyzer explanation to identify the configuration element preventing the expected path.
recommended_checks: Identify the component or explanation code reported by Reachability Analyzer
Determine whether the blocker is a route table, Security Group, Network ACL, gateway, peering connection, Transit Gateway, or another supported component
Return to the relevant troubleshooting section instead of changing unrelated components
Re-run the analysis after the configuration is corrected

analyze_flow_log_reject.title: VPC Flow Logs Show REJECT
analyze_flow_log_reject.purpose: Observed traffic reached a logged VPC interface or boundary but was rejected by the evaluated network controls.
recommended_checks: Confirm source IP, destination IP, protocol and ports in the Flow Log record
Confirm the Flow Log timestamp matches the test
Check Security Group rules for the relevant resource
Check Network ACL rules for the relevant subnet
Correlate the reject with the exact direction of the traffic

check_workload_or_return_path.title: AWS Network Path Appears Reachable
check_workload_or_return_path.purpose: AWS configuration analysis indicates a valid network path, so continue with return-path, operating-system, listening-service, or application troubleshooting.
likely_causes: Operating-system firewall
Application not listening on the expected port
Wrong bind address
Asymmetric or missing return route outside the analyzed path
Application-level failure
Incorrect DNS destination
Workload health issue
recommended_checks: Verify the application is listening on the intended IP and port
Check the instance operating-system firewall
Check the destination workload health
Verify the reverse path
Confirm DNS resolves to the expected destination
Use packet capture or host-level tools where appropriate

aws_network_path_working.title: AWS Network Path Appears to Be Working
aws_network_path_working.purpose: The AWS networking evidence indicates that traffic is accepted and the expected virtual network path is available.
recommended_checks: Confirm the application itself is healthy
Verify host operating-system networking
Verify DNS if a hostname is used
Check application logs and listening sockets
Preserve the network evidence showing the AWS path is functioning

check_vpc_route.title: Check VPC-to-VPC Routing
check_vpc_route.purpose: Verify that the source VPC route table sends the destination VPC prefix toward the intended VPC Peering Connection or Transit Gateway.
recommended_checks: Identify the source subnet route table
Find the most specific route matching the destination VPC CIDR
Confirm the route target is the expected VPC Peering Connection or Transit Gateway
Verify the destination VPC has a return route toward the source VPC CIDR
Check for overlapping CIDR ranges
Confirm the route table associated with the actual workload subnet is the one being reviewed

check_vpc_peering.title: Check VPC Peering Path
check_vpc_peering.purpose: Verify that the VPC Peering Connection is usable and that both VPCs have the required routes for bidirectional communication.
recommended_checks: Confirm the VPC Peering Connection is active
Verify the source VPC route table points the destination CIDR to the peering connection
Verify the destination VPC route table points the source CIDR to the peering connection
Confirm the VPC CIDR ranges do not overlap
After routing is confirmed, validate Security Groups and Network ACLs on the destination path

check_tgw_attachment.title: Check Transit Gateway Attachment
check_tgw_attachment.purpose: Verify that the source and destination networks are correctly attached to the Transit Gateway and are using the intended Transit Gateway route-table relationships.
recommended_checks: Confirm the source VPC attachment is available
Confirm the destination VPC or VPN attachment is available
Identify the Transit Gateway route table associated with the source attachment
Verify the destination prefix exists in that Transit Gateway route table
Check whether the destination attachment is propagated to the required Transit Gateway route table
Verify the return direction uses the appropriate association and route propagation
Confirm the VPC subnet route tables point the remote prefixes toward the Transit Gateway

check_hybrid_attachment.title: Check Hybrid AWS Attachment
check_hybrid_attachment.purpose: Identify whether on-premises connectivity reaches AWS through a Site-to-Site VPN attached to a Virtual Private Gateway or Transit Gateway.
recommended_checks: Identify whether the VPN terminates on a Virtual Private Gateway or Transit Gateway
Confirm the AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection exists
Check both VPN tunnel states
Determine whether routing uses static routes or BGP
Confirm the on-premises and AWS CIDR ranges expected across the VPN
Identify the VPC subnet route table used by the destination workload

check_vgw_vpn.title: Check Virtual Private Gateway VPN Path
check_vgw_vpn.purpose: Verify Site-to-Site VPN state and routing when the VPN terminates on a Virtual Private Gateway.
recommended_checks: Confirm at least one Site-to-Site VPN tunnel is UP
For dynamic routing, confirm BGP is established and expected prefixes are advertised and received
For static routing, confirm the expected static prefixes are configured
Verify the VPC subnet route table contains the on-premises prefix
If route propagation is used, confirm Virtual Private Gateway propagation is enabled on the relevant route table
Verify the customer gateway has a return route toward the AWS VPC CIDR

check_tgw_vpn.title: Check Transit Gateway VPN Path
check_tgw_vpn.purpose: Verify Site-to-Site VPN routing when the VPN terminates on an AWS Transit Gateway.
recommended_checks: Confirm at least one VPN tunnel is UP
For dynamic routing, verify BGP session state and advertised/received prefixes
Confirm the VPN attachment is associated with the intended Transit Gateway route table
Confirm VPN routes are propagated or statically present in the required Transit Gateway route table
Confirm the destination VPC attachment is reachable through that Transit Gateway route table
Verify the destination VPC subnet route table points the on-premises prefix toward the Transit Gateway
Verify the on-premises router has a return route toward the AWS VPC CIDR

vpc_cidr_overlap_failure.title: Overlapping VPC CIDR Problem
vpc_cidr_overlap_failure.purpose: The VPC addressing plan prevents the expected straightforward routed connectivity.
likely_causes: Source and destination VPC CIDR ranges overlap
A destination prefix is ambiguous because of overlapping address space
recommended_checks: Confirm both VPC CIDR ranges
Review the addressing design
Determine whether renumbering, NAT, or an alternate architecture is required

vpc_peering_failure.title: VPC Peering Failure
vpc_peering_failure.purpose: The expected VPC Peering Connection is not currently usable.
recommended_checks: Verify peering connection state
Verify both VPC route tables
Verify non-overlapping CIDRs
Verify destination Security Groups and Network ACLs after peering is restored

tgw_attachment_failure.title: Transit Gateway Attachment Failure
tgw_attachment_failure.purpose: One or more required Transit Gateway attachments are not in the expected state.
recommended_checks: Verify source attachment state
Verify destination attachment state
Confirm the correct VPC/VPN resources are attached
Verify accepted/shared attachment state for cross-account designs

tgw_route_table_failure.title: Transit Gateway Routing Failure
tgw_route_table_failure.purpose: Transit Gateway routing does not provide the expected path between attachments.
likely_causes: Wrong Transit Gateway route-table association
Route propagation disabled or missing
Destination prefix missing
Static route points to the wrong attachment
Return direction uses a different route table without the required route
recommended_checks: Identify the Transit Gateway route table associated with the source attachment
Verify the destination prefix
Verify the destination attachment target
Review propagations
Repeat the same analysis for the return direction

site_to_site_vpn_failure.title: AWS Site-to-Site VPN Failure
site_to_site_vpn_failure.purpose: The AWS Site-to-Site VPN or its routing adjacency is not fully operational.
recommended_checks: Check both tunnel states
Verify IKE and IPsec state on the customer gateway
For BGP, verify neighbor state and advertisements
For static routing, verify configured prefixes
Review AWS Site-to-Site VPN logs if enabled
Verify both directions of routing before changing security controls

hybrid_return_path_failure.title: Hybrid Return Path Failure
hybrid_return_path_failure.purpose: The forward path reaches AWS but the on-premises or AWS return route does not correctly return traffic to the source.
likely_causes: On-premises route to AWS CIDR is missing
AWS route to on-premises CIDR is missing
BGP advertisement missing in one direction
Different VPN/TGW path selected on return
Asymmetric routing through another firewall or WAN path
recommended_checks: Verify the AWS route toward the on-premises prefix
Verify the on-premises route toward the AWS prefix
Compare BGP advertisements and learned routes in both directions
Check whether the forward and reverse paths use the same expected VPN/TGW architecture
Correlate firewall session state where applicable
